abstract_research_topics.justification: Wavelet scattering is a mathematical framework that extends wavelet transforms by incorporating a hierarchy of convolutions and modulus operators, often used to create features invariant to certain transformations, and is hence an abstract research topic.
Scattering transform is a theoretical framework in signal processing, widely used to build invariant and stable signal representations, making it an abstract research topic.
Similarly to scattering transform, scattering transforms refer to the collection of methods used to obtain hierarchical and invariant representations, contributing to abstract research topics.
Faultload benchmarking deals with the theoretical aspect of evaluating system performance under certain conditions, which is often abstract and not necessarily linked to practical applications.

Benchmarking is a broad term often used in the evaluation and comparison of models or systems. It has both theoretical and practical aspects but leans towards abstract research in the context of evaluating algorithms.

Deep learning compilers are involved in the optimization and transformation of high-level DL models into executable code, rooted in systems and computational theory, and hence are part of abstract research.
Testing of deep neural networks includes theoretical aspects of verifying and validating the models for robustness and accuracy, therefore aligning more with abstract research topics.
